name: cer-ja-roundtrip
metric: round-trip CER (docs/evaluation.md §2): musculus synthesis → ruler ASR transcription → CER. Two flavours: text-level (cer_normalized, orthography noise included) and reading-level (both sides through the same ja frontend, homophone-fair phoneme comparison)

ruler.adapter: euhadra 0.3 (crates.io) ParakeetAdapter — the same model euhadra's L1 uses for ja
ruler.audio_condition: 44100 Hz decode output, FFT-resampled (rubato) to 16 kHz mono

condition.dictionary: none (baseline measures the bare frontend; --dict runs are separate rows)

per_item_highlights: plain sentences (今日はいい天気ですね / 午前10時 / 1,200円 / 50m / 12枚 / musculus文): text CER 0.000–0.048, reading CER 0.000
猫が座って動かない: text CER 0.667 (ASR wrote kana) but reading CER 0.000 — the orthography/intelligibility split the two metrics exist for
成功率は5%上がりました: text CER 0.667, reading CER 0.192 — the percent-symbol gap does real damage (worklist)
2026年2月14日: reading CER 0.018 — the date-compound gap (とし/つき) is acoustically visible (worklist)
Wi-Fi: reading CER 0.312 — ruler transcribed Latin 'wi-fi', whose letter-reading differs from the spoken ワイファイ; a known NJD-on-hypothesis noise source, not a synthesis defect

tolerance_policy.relative: regression flag if mean reading CER exceeds 0.050 * 1.25 on the same ruler version and sentence set
tolerance_policy.absolute: mean reading CER must stay below 0.15; mean RTF must stay below 0.5 on the reference hardware

notes: Reading CER is the primary intelligibility number; text CER is kept for literature comparability and to catch orthography-level drift.
The percent/date rows quantify the L3 gap worklist acoustically — ΔCER after each normalization fix lands here as a new row.
The ruler is shared with euhadra's L1 (same model + adapter), so ja CER numbers are comparable across the two projects.
Manual run only (2.4 GB ruler): cargo run --release --features onnx,wav --example eval_cer -- --json docs/benchmarks/cer-ja/run.json
